first_impression: Pretty, cosy and clearly made with love: the title screen and the sunset cutaways look like postcards, and there is a real season here with a different twist every evening. The problem is that from the footage, a lot of the actual playing is me watching a small white blob of sheep creep across a big flat field while the dog trots behind it.
best_things: The sunset cutaways (00:42, 03:54, 07:57, 11:45) and the title screen are lovely, and the First Snow evening (11:09 to 12:33), with its teal stream, black sheep and falling snow, is the screenshot that would make me click.

The season feels like a real campaign: a map of nine evenings, stars, ribbons and unlockable charms ('Evening 2 is open', 'New charm: Swift Paws' at 01:42), and each evening adds something new: a sheepdog trial with gates, lambs, Old Angus the ram, mist, a storm that floods the ford, snow, and a night watch until dawn.

The wolf snatches are clear and tense: a red banner with the distance and the seconds left, a small 'Snatch!' camera inset, a sprint over the bridge and then 'Sheep rescued!' (05:06 to 05:12, 10:27 to 10:36).

worst_problems.problem: Long dead stretches where almost nothing changes on screen: the dog stands or creeps behind a small clump of sheep that inches along, and frame after frame looks the same. The camera is far out, so the 'action' is a tiny white blob moving slowly across a big lawn.
worst_problems.suggestion: Make driving a settled flock quicker, or put more in the way while you drive (a sheep breaking off, a gap in a wall, a gully to get around), so the minutes between the wolves are not just walking.

worst_problems.problem: In the Glenbrae Trial the sheep bunch up at the pen mouth for 20+ seconds and won't go in. It looks like the fiddly, frustrating part of the trial, and the clip ends with them still outside.
worst_problems.suggestion: Make the pen easier to read and to work: a clearer gate opening, the sheep reacting more to small moves of the dog right at the mouth, or a visible 'pressure' cue showing which way they will step.

worst_problems.problem: The mist evening is a beige-pink haze over the whole screen. It reads less like fog and more like a dirty filter, everything is low contrast, and with the stray-sheep icons stacking up on the left edge it is hard to see anything interesting for a whole evening.
worst_problems.suggestion: Keep a clear, crisp bubble around Pip and let the fog roll in thick banks with gaps instead of a flat wash, and give the moor some silhouettes (cairns, a dyke, trees) that loom out of it.

worst_problems.problem: Bright glowing yellow orbs keep appearing on the ground, and the game never explains them. They look like a pickup, a bug or a lens flare stuck to the field.
worst_problems.suggestion: If it is something I can interact with, label it or show it on the tutorial card; if it is just a firefly or a glint, make it much smaller and softer.

worst_problems.problem: At dusk the meadow turns a muddy mustard-brown, with lilac heather blotches and dark smears that look like spilled paint, not a sunset glow. Several evenings end up looking the same dull ochre.
worst_problems.suggestion: Keep the grass reading as grass at sunset (warm light on green, cool shade) and give each place its own dusk colour, so Loch Ailsa and the corrie do not both turn the same brown.

boredom_points: 01:06 to 01:30: almost half a minute of the dog standing at the left and five sheep standing in the middle, with only the timer changing.
04:33 to 05:00: walking the flock along the stream beside the bridge, eight nearly identical frames before the wolf shows up.
07:42 to 08:57: the whole mist evening is the same beige screen, a dog pushing a clump along a track, crossing a bridge, and pushing again.
The six-second sunset cutaway (03:54 to 03:57) is gorgeous the first few times but would get old on the ninth evening if I cannot skip it.
Long drives across snow along the track (11:30 to 11:42, 12:36 to 12:51) look nice but there is nothing to do except hold a direction.
confusions: What are the glowing yellow balls on the ground?
In the night watch the moonlit rocks look like round white sheep or eggs (13:15 to 13:21); I could not tell rocks from strays at a glance.
White sheep on white snow (11:12 to 12:33) only stand out by their outlines; in busier moments I would lose track of which blob was a sheep and which was a snowy rock or bush.
The sheep-head icons stacked along the left edge in the mist (07:24, 08:12, 08:21): are those sheep I have lost, bleats I heard, or directions to go?
At 10:57 the whole screen goes almost pure white; I assume it is lightning, but in the footage it looks like the game blew out.
Night watch at 13:24: 'Something big crashes through the bracken' and the flock scatters, but I never saw what it was.
In the trial the gates are thin posts that are hard to spot on the plain lawn; without the labels I would not have known where to drive.
wish_list: A photo mode, because the sunset and snow shots deserve it.
Online leaderboards or a daily challenge for the trial scores and best times.
Cosmetic unlocks for Pip (collars, other coat colours, other breeds) to go with the charms.
Local co-op with two dogs working the same flock.
An endless or free-herding mode once the season is done.
A skip button for cutaways, and a closer default camera option that still keeps the flock in view.
one_line_review: A gorgeous, cosy sheepdog season with real wolf panic and a new twist every evening, but bring patience: a lot of it is nudging a white blob across a big lawn.
